The Committee on Lodge Financing:
The Committee on Lodge Financing, and each of its members in·
dividually. as opposed to Resolution No. 3 and recommend a no vote
for the following reasons :
The "Whereas" clauses of the resolution do not set forth sufficient
grounds to support the resolution.
The resolution would put Grand Lodge into the lending business,
for which business it is not properly equipped. The Committee handling
the loans would be required to retain professional appraisers, set up a
collection system, establish interest rates required, establish local in·
spection and loan investigation systems. and , in general, esta blish or
hire the personnel a nd business system necessary to make and service
real estate loans.
Under the plan, Grand Lodge would have available approximately
$250,000.00 per year for this purpose. The Committee or Trustees of
the fund therefore would undoubtedly be required to pick and choose
among applicants for the loans . A general feeling of ill- will would be
created, contrary to the basic principles of Free Masonry.

The Committee qn Finance:
There has been referred to the Committee on Finance Resolution No.
3 relating to the creation of a fund designed to serve as a so-called mortgage bank for constituent Lodges.
The resolution spea ks of surplus funds being invested by trustees of
such funds in s uch a manner as to earn the highest ra te of interes t or
dividends, for investments to be made in a manner as to make the principal of the fu nd available a t all times for the p urpose of making interestfree loans as needed, a nd for investments to be made on the advice of
the Finance Committee as and w hen required. We point out that the
investment of Grand Lodge fu nds is made by the Investment Committee
an d it is to be assu med that investment of monies in a fund s uch as the
one proposed in this resolution would have to be assigned to the In vestment Committee as provided by Section 245 C .M.C.
Grand Lodge, as a proposed mortgage lender, would no doubt be
called upon to consider requests for the refinancing of mortgages already made by private lenders. Obviously, Lodges which have outstand·
ing obligations would be most anxious to be relieved of onerous interest
burdens. Grand Lodge would need to adopt a proper method of securing

234

PROCEEDINGS op· THE

GRAND LODGE OF CALIFORNIA

loans to Lodges and be prepared to enforce loan repayments from time
to time; otherwise Grand Lodge could become the eventual owner of
constituent Lodge properties.
If the resolution has merit, and it is the conclusion of the Finance
Committee that it does not, loans to Lodges would have to be secured in
a safe and prudent manner, and amortization or repayment of loans
should be on a basis consistent for all Lodges.
All records relating to the granting of loans to Lodges, the collection
of payments, and the multitudinous details would have to be maintained
in the Grand Secretary's office and be reviewed by Grand Lodge auditors. Notwithstanding that the resolution provides for certain administrative charges to recipient Lodges. the Finance Committee is concerned
with the burden to be imposed upon the Grand Secretary's office and
with the expenses to be incurred by fund trustees should this resolution
be approved, all of which would have to be met by all Lodges through
the Grand Lodge additional per capita tax, even though all Lodges will
not, or cannot. avail themselves of the proposed fund's benefits.
The Finance Committee regards as wholly inequitable the thought
that Advisory Committees or Trustees would be empowered to grant
flexible terms to Lodges seeking financing. thus creating dissatisfaction
on the part of Lodges which do not receive terms as favorable as others.
Your Committee on Finance recommends a no vote.
The Committees on Jurisprudence and on Policy and General Purposes indicated their concurrence in the recommendations.
A majority voted against the resolution.

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that. in view 0£ the importance
0£ an approved Decision of a Grand Master, it having the effect of law,

The Committee on Jurisprudence:
Your Committee on Jurisprudence has read and considered R esolution No. 5, which proposes in part to amend Section 70 of the California
Masonic Code by adding thereto a sentence read ing, "Any decision of
a Grand Mas ter, when and as adopted by Gra nd Lodge, becomes an
edict of Grand Lodge."
Such an amendment is entirely redundant and unnecessary as the
Grand M aster's decisions, w hen approved by Grand Lodge. are adopted
by resolution and Section 70 presently provides that any resolution
passed by the Grand Lodge is a regulation thereof, a nd thus becomes
part of the body of Masonic law .
Resolution No. 5 also provides, in effect, tha t any Grand Master's
decision, which is not repeti tive of something already codified, must be
submitted to the Grand Secretary 90 days before the Grand Lodge's
Annual Communication or it cannot be acted upon until the Annual
Communication of the nex t succeeding year.
We are unalterably opposed to such a provision. Some of th e Grand
Master's decisions will be rendered or possibly altered within the 90 day
period prior to Grand Lodg e and all of his decisions should be acted
upon by the Communication over which he presides and at the earliest
possible time. It would add nothing but confusion and uncertainty to
require that these decisions be left una pproved by Grand Lodge for over
a year and until the next Annual Communication.
We move the adoption of the resolution and recommend a no vote.
A majority voted against the resolution.

a new sentence shall be added to Section 781 of the California Masonic
Code, reading, "Any Decision 0£ a Grand Master, except those which
are repetitive of matters already codified, shall not receive the approval
0£ Grand Lodge and be codified, unless such Decision shall have been
submitted to the Grand Secretary in accordance with the provisions of
this Section; all others shall be unfinished business to be taken up for

WILSON 0 . WADE, P .M., No. 328
Referred to Committees on Jurisprudence and on P olicy and General
Purposes.
The Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
The only policy question involved in this resolution is found in the
concluding paragraph which provides, in effect, that any decision of a
Grand Master, except those repetitive 0£ matters already codified, shall
not receive the approval of Grand Lodge unless such decision shall have
been submitted to the Grand Secretary at least ninety days prior to the
commencement date of the next Annual Communication.
There is a fundamental difference between a decision of the Grand
Master interpreting existing law and a resolution seeking to change the
law. When the Grand Master is called upon to render a decision he
interprets the existing la w as set forth in our Constitution and Ordinances in light of the facts presented. Conversely, a resolution, presumably, changes or alters the existing law. In this latter case the brethren
should have an opportunity to view and consider in advance the proposed changes in the law. But your Policy Committee believes tha t such
advance notification is not necessary for decisions of the Grand Master
which only interpret existing law.
A resolution can be prepared in advance without difficulty. This is
not necessarily true of the decisions of the Grand Master. A situation
may develop within ninety days of the Annual Communication which
requires the Gra nd M aster to render his decision on an important matter.
This decision, except by emergent procedure, would remain unapproved
or in limbo for a period in excess of one year. Such uncertainty on
important matters is undesirable.
Lastly the resolution would crea te two classes of decisions; those
which are repetitive of matters already in the annotations and those
decisions which are not repetitive. If a decision is in one class it would
have to be filed with the Grand Secretary; if in the other class, it would
not have to be filed. Two classes of decisions would create confusion in
the law of Grand Lodge and the resolution fails to provide who would
decide, as to each decision, in which class it would fall.
The Committee on Policy and General Purposes recommends a no
vote.

CERTIFICATE OF RECOGNITION (6)

LONG SERVICE

T o the M ost Worshipful Grand Lodge F. & A. M . of California:
WHEREAS : It has been a custom among the fraternity of F ree and
Accepted M asons from time immemorial, at th e request of a Master in
recognition of long-rendered service to his Lodge on the part of a deserving brother in such capacities as secretary, treasurer, tiler, chaplain,
officers' coach, head candidates' coach, master pro tern at fu nerals, to
petition the Grand Master to pass the chair which entitled that brother
to part of the rights and honors and to enable him to gain further light
in the capacity of virtual Pas t Master which in no way entitled him to
the rights and prerogatives of an actual Past M aster; and
WHEREAS: It is against the teachings and precepts of the Grand
Lodge of Free and Accepted Masons of the State of California to confer
such a title as virtual Past M aster; and
WHEREAS : There a re deserving brothers of some special recognition of long and satisfactory service rendered to many of our Lodges;

BE IT THEREFORE RESOLVED: That the Grand Lodge of
Free and Accepted Masons of the State of California devise and design

served their Lodges in a capacity such as stated above;
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED: That these certificates be awarded upon due petition by the Master of the Lodge served by the deserving

The Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
Your Committee on Policy and General Purposes, to which Resolution No. 6 entitled "Certificate of Recognition-Long Service" has been
referred, reports as follows:
The preamble of this resolution reminds us of the many brothers who
have rendered long and distinguished service to their several Lodges,
and the resolution itself would have Grand Lodge devise and design a
certificate of recognition as well as a suitable ritual for its presentation.
It also would place upon the Grand Master the duty of approving each
application for such a certificate.
Your Committee is pleased to note that the Lodge officers of the
many deserving and long serving brothers are anxious to confer a special award upon them, but we feel that there are many other more personal ways of expressing appreciation to them, such as a special evening
in their honor with their many friends present. We feel that a ritualistic
presentation of another certificate to add to an already bulging card case
is not the .m ost appropriate means. We also hesitate to recommend a
plan which would add another burden to an already overworked Grand
Master, or another ritual to be memorized by Lodge officers.
The Committee on Ritual concurs in this report.
We, therefore, move the adoption of this resolution, but the Committee on Policy and General Purposes recommends a no vote.
A majority voted against the resolution.

CERTIFICATE OF RECOGNITION CANDIDATES COACHES
(7)
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, most important to Freemasonry are the teachings that
have been handed down since the days of King Solomon, and
WHEREAS, the Fraternity holds in just respect and honors each
year the teachers in our Public Schools, and
WHEREAS, wtihin our own Fraternity are brethren who year after
year give of their time and effort to act as candidate's coaches, thereby
becoming teachers of Freemasonry, and
WHEREAS, without these dedicated brethren the Fraternity would
soon cease to exist, and
WHEREAS, the Fraternity should endeavor to honor its own teachers in some way,
NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED:
That the Grand Lodge cause to be printed and made available to
constituent Lodges a suitable certificate*, which the constituent Lodges
shall be permitted to confer upon candidate's coaches at the discretion
of the Master of a cons tituent Lodge; which will in a small way acknowledge the brotherly love and affection that is evidenced by said coaches
in giving of their time and effort and becoming teachers within our Fraternity.

The Committee on Ritual:
The Committee on Ritual, to which has been presented Resolution
No. 7, reports as follows:
Resolution No. 7 proposes "That the Grand Lodge cause to be
printed and made available to constituent Lodges a suitable certificate.
which the constituent Lodges shall be permitted to confer upon candidate's coaches at the discretion of the Master of a constituent Lodge;
which will in a small way acknowledge the brotherly love and affection
that is evidenced by said coaches in giving of their time and effort and
becoming teachers within our Fraternity ."
At the 1962 Communication of this Grand Lodge, the then Grand
Lecturer, Very Worshipful Donald G . Campbell, in his annual report
outlined the program for candidate education to be utilized in the con-

PROCEEDINGS OF THE

GRAND LODGE OP CALIFORNIA

stituent Lodges through the use of the Handbook for Candidate Coaches.
The program, adopted by this Grand Lodge, provides that "candidates'
coaches be presented , after properly qualifying, with a certificate of recognition, as well as a copy of the Candidates Coaches Handbook."
The program was put into effect in 1963, with the Senior Warden,
representing the Master, being in charge of the program of candidate
education, supervised by the Inspector of the District. An appropriate
"Certificate of Qualification and Appointment" is included in the Handbook. to be signed by the Senior Warden as Recommender, appointed
and signed by the Master, and approved by the Inspector of the District.
The program now in effect sets certain standards for qualifying for
the Certificate of Qualification and Appointment, both from the standpoint of ritual and Masonic information. The certificate is not conferred
at the discretion of the Master or any other person - it is earned in
accordance with an established program.
In view of the conflict between this Resolution and an already established procedure of recognition of our Candidates Coaches which is more
comprehensive in scope, we recommend a no vote.
The Committee on Policy and General Purposes indicated its concurrence in the recommendation.

FUNERAL SERVICE-FAMILY COPY
(8)
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge F. & A. M . of California:
WHEREAS. there is no provision in the California Masonic Code
for the presentation of the Masonic Funeral Service in appropriate pamphlet form to the widow or next of kin of the deceased brother, and,
WHEREAS. the funeral service as revised by Grand Lodge,
F. & A. M. of California, October, 1955, is ritual, yet monitorial, and
contains some of the most beautiful words and phrases written, and,
WHEREAS. at the time of funeral services it may be presumed this
fine Masonic service is beard and perhaps soon forgotten by the widow
or next of kin due to grief and sorrow, and,
WHEREAS. at a later date when the widow or next of kin may
wish to reflect on what was spoken during the funeral service, they cannot recall anything except that it was beautiful.

The Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
Proposed Resolution No. 9 would authorize the presentation of special aprons to past elected Grand Lodge Officers who have not served
as Grand Master. While your committee agrees that suitable recognition of the services of distinguishe d brethren is both appropriate and
desirable, we feel that the proposal set forth in Resolution No. 9 is
impractical and could lead to a burdensome and complicated multiplicity
of designs, emblems and awards. This Grand Lodge has no prescribed
emblem for any of the past grand offices named in the resolution. The
awarding of special aprons to these past grand officers may very properly lead to the presentation of special aprons, and with them the accompanying special emblem designs, to certain of the appointive Grand
Lodge officers who have served our Grand Lodge in able fashion--or
even to all who have been appointed as Grand Lodge officers. If Grand
Lodge sets a pattern for this form of recognition, then the same recognition might properly be given to constituent Lodge officers who have
not served as Master of their Lodge. We are authorized to report that
the Jurisprudence Committee states there is no legal question involved,
and we are also authorized to state that the Finance Committee. concurs
with this report.
We move the adoption of the resolution and recommend a no vote.
A majority voted against the resolution.

The Committee on Finance:
There has been referred to the Committee on Finance Resolution
No. 10 calling for a new Grand Lodge committee to meet annually in
San Francisco, at an appropriate and convenient time, for the purpose
of determining the name or names of one or more brothers to be placed
in nomination for the office of Junior Grand Warden of this Grand
Lodge at each Annual Communication.
The expense to be incurred annually as this proposed committee
meets cannot be determined in advance. An eighteen member committee, to be assembled from different sections of our jurisdiction, which
could include Hawaii on occasion, would have to plan a minimum of one
full day for deliberations, possibly more. Members from some areas
would have to arrive in San Francisco by the evening preceding the
day set for the meeting in order to be available for the meeting. For a
committee of the size proposed, it is quite probable that discussions and
determination of the name or names of candidates could not be concluded in one day. Its establishment as a Grand Lodge Standing Committee, or as a Special Committee, would have a bearing on the amount
to be appropriated for the committee. A conservative estimate of the
annual expense to be incurred would be $3500.00.
It is the opinion of this Committee that no new benefit or service will
accrue to Grand Lodge by the adoption of this resolution. The annual
cost to Grand Lodge, as indicated, will be sizeable and we must recommend a no vote.

In our opinion the past and present practice whereby the names of
brethren qualified for election as Junior Grand Warden have been
brought to the attention of Grand Lodge members has worked out well
and over the years has resulted in the election of a succession of men
whose devoted service to the Craft has been invaluable. By their experience our Past Grand Masters are better qualified than any other group
to recommend the names of qualified brethren. In contrast, we believe
it would be extremely improbable that officers of constituent Lodges in
northern California who would be members of a Nominating Committee,
would be sufficiently cognizant of the qualifications of a brother from a
Southern California Lodge to cast an intelligent vote for his nomination
as Junior Grand Warden; and, of course, the reverse would be true of
committee members from the south as to prospective Junior Grand
Wardens from the north.

in their jurisdictions. In at least one of the few Grand Lodges where

advertising the merits of candidates for election to Grand Lodge offices;
some candidates have been known to hold campaign dinner meetings or
stag parties at which liquid refreshments of some potency were dispensed .

To the Most Worshi pful Grand Lodge F. & A. M. of California:
BE IT RESOL VED. that Section 375 of the Californ ia Masoni c
Code be amende d to read as follows:
Sec. 375. Two or more Lodges, located near each other, may consolidate into one upon such terms as may be agreed upon between the
Lodges . There shall first be adopted by each Lodge at a Stated Meeting
a Resolut ion to the effect that a consolid ation is expedie nt, and that Committees be appoint ed to meet and arrange terms. Notice in writing of
the adoptio n of such Resolut ion shall be given to all member s of the
Lodge forthwi th. Such Commi ttees must agree upon the terms and report in writing to their respecti ve Lodges at a stated meeting, and the
reports must be received and concurr ed in by the respective Lodges. The
signatu re of at least three-fo urths of the members of each Lodge shall be
obtaine d to a paper or papers substan tially in this form: "In pursuan ce
of certain action of.. .......... Lodge No ........... .. and ................ Lodge No.
........... tending to the consolid ation of said Lodges into one Lodge, under
the name and number of ............ Lodge No ............ . ,we, the undersi gned.
member s of ............ Lodge No .......... do hereby express our assent to
and our desire for such propose d consolid ation." (Standa rd Forms to be
used will be made availab le by the Grand Secreta ry's office.)
At a stated meeting not earlier than the third stated meeting after
adoptio n of the first Resolut ion, the Master of each Lodge shall canvass
the consent s of members of his Lodge. and if he finds the required number of consent s have been properl y signed, he shall decla re the consolid ation to be approve d by said Lodge. When all proceed ings are complet ed,
they shall be entered upon the records of the existing Lodges. The written consent s and a certificate of proceed ings and action taken by the
Lodges must then be certified to the Grand Secreta ry by the respecti ve
Secreta ries under the seals of their respecti ve Lodges. If the Grand Master shall find it impract icable for a Lodge to secure the requisit e written
consent s, he may approve the consolid ation upon the written consent of
not less than a majority of the member s of each Lodge.
The Lodge thus formed may bear the name and number of one of the
Lodges compos ing it. in which case it may retain the Charter and Seal
of that Lodge; or it may bear the name of one and the number of another
of such Lodges and shall then receive a new Charter without charge.
and provide a new Seal; or it may have an endorse ment of the authoriz ation of such consolid ation by the Grand Lodge made upon the Charter
of one of the compon ent Lodges.
No such consolid ation shall go into effect until all the proceed ings
relative thereto shall have been submitt ed to and approve d by the Grand

Respect fully submitt ed,

QUALIFICATIONS - LODGE OFFICERS
(18)
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, proficiency in the candidates lecture before an Entered
Apprentice can be passed or a Fellowcraft can be raised is required; and
WHEREAS, the members of the several constituent Lodges look to
their officers to be proficient in the ritual and assist in the learning of the
candidate's lectures of the severa l degrees; and
WHEREAS. the members appointed and elected to serve in each of
the several offices in the constituent Lodges of this jurisdiction should
on their installation to such office be proficient in the ritual of the several
degrees required by such office;
NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that the appropriate
sections of the California Masonic Code be amended so as to provide,
"Before any member of a constituent Lodge of this jurisdiction shall be
appointed or elected to any office other than Treasurer. Secretary, Organist or Tyler in such Lodge he shall by examination in open Lodge
show his proficiency in the Candidate's Lecture of the Third Degree."
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED. that this resolution shall become
effective at the election or appointment of officers next following the Annual Communication at which such resolution shall be passed,
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED. that this resolution shall not pertain to any officer elected or appointed before this resolution is passed.
Jurns J. DEMooR. M .. No. 633
Referred to Committees on Jurisprudence. on Policy and General
Purposes. and on Ritual.
The Committee on Ritual:
The Committee on Ritual, to which has been presented Resolution
No. 18, reports as fellows :
Resolution No. 18 proposes that "before any member of a constituent
Lodge of this jurisdiction shall be appointed or elected to any office other
than Treasurer, Secretary. Organist, or Tiler in such Lodge, he shall by
examination in open Lodge show his proficiency in the Candidate's Lecture of the Third Degree."
The proficiency of our newly raised brethren in the lecture of the
Third Degree has concerned this Grand Lodge for many years. Resolutions have been introduced from time is time to require proficiency, but
have been defeated as either impractical or unenforceable. The one exception is the provision embodied in Question 15 of our Application for
Degrees form. which requires proficiency in the Candidate's Lecture of
the Degree of Master Mason before applying for membership in any
Lodge. order. or organization, the prerequisite of membership wherein
is that a person be a Master Mason.
The Ritual Committee has for many years been concerned with the

PROCEED INGS OF THE

GRAND LODGE OF CALIFOR NIA

instruction of the Candid ate, not only in the required Lecture proficiencies, but also in the whole area of Masoni c instructio~ and. educatio n of
the Candid ate, while under the tutelage of the Candid ates coach. We
feel that the implem entation of the progres s through the us.e of the
H andboo k for C andidat es Coache s at the local Lodge level will go far
toward achievin g the objectiv es of this Resolut ion.
W e are opposed to the Resolut ion as present ed for several reasons .
Our principa l objectio n is based on the effect the provisio n of this
Resolution would have upon the small Lodges, particul arly those in the
rural, mounta inous, and remote areas of the jurisdic tion, where in some
instance s the local residen ts of the Lodge member ship are barely sufficient in numbers to fill the Lodge offices each year. The proficiency requirement would preclud e the filling of the offices in many instance s.
Second ly, there is a trend to confine the progres sive line of offices to
the Junior and Senior Deacon s, Junior and Senior Warde ns. and Master,
with other offices being filled on an underst ood one year basis. This resolution would require that the latter, the Junior and Senior Ste~a~ds,
Marsha l, and Chaplai n, even though serving only one year at the mv1tation of the Master, would be required to have passed a proficie ncy examinati on in the Candid ate's Lecture of the Third Degree in order to
assist and serve during the year.
Finally, we feel that even though the intent of the Resolution has
merit, from a practica l standpo int the officer who progres ses thr~ugh the
various proficiencies required for advance ment t~rough the Se.mar ~ea­

Senior officers and M asters of our Lodges, because the ma jority have
passed their Third Degree proficiency before progres sing to the higher
offices.

Referred to Committe es on Jurisprude nce. and on Policy and General
Purposes.
The Committe e on Policy and General Purposes:
Your Committe e on Policy and General Purposes, to which was
referred Resolution No. 19, reports as follows:
Resolution No. 19 proposes that : "No Mason shall hold office in any
capacity in any ,y outh organizati on wherein the prerequisi te is that he
be a M aster Mason, except that he shall have presented himself before
the Worshipf ul Master of the Lodge in whose jurisdictio n the meeting
place of the organizati on lies, and have satisfied said Worshipf ul Master
as to his proficiency in the C .M .C. and in our ancient usages and customs. to the extent that his incumbenc y in such position shall bring no
discredit or embarrass ment to the Craft." "No Mason, holding such
an office shall continue to hold such office except at the pleasure of said
Worshipf ul Master."
In the event of concurren t jurisdiction, the Inspector( s) of the District ( s) involved shall rule which M aster shall have jurisdictio n."
A reading of this language of the "Resolved " clause leads to two
observatio ns:
First, the proposal would subject any Master Mason who has volunteered his services for the promotion of youth groups, the existence and
encourage ment of which have long been the policy of this Grand Lodge,

to a~. u~limited inquisition by the Master of a Lodge. No standards of
fam1hanty with the complexit ies of the C.M.C. or the history, nature
and pur~oses. of ancient Masonic usages and customs is provided. Absolute discretion as to the degree of technical Masonic law, decisions
and usages required is left to the examining Master. What he required
of one examiner could vary completely from what he required from anot~e~. 1:he result could well be utter confusion and widesprea d discr1mmation.
The second obvious observatio n is that even if any Master Mason
could c~nceivably pass the unrestricte d examinati on permitted, he would
at all times the~eafter be permitted to continue his youth work only so
long as the whim of the Master let him do so. In short, the M aster is
made an absolute czar whose control of the youth organizati on would
thereby be establishe d for all time.
This Grand Lodge has never sought any such absolute control of
the youth organizati ons which it fosters. It should not begin now.
For these reasons your Committe e on Policy and General Purposes
moves the adoption of Resolution No. 19, but strongly urges a no vote.
The. Committe e on Jurisprudence indicated its concurren ce in the recommendation .
A majority voted against the resolution.

Referred to Committees on Ju risprudence, on Policy and General
Purposes, and on Ritual.

The Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
Resolution number 20 proposes to change our present law in the particular under which an applicant for the degrees who must rely upon a
hea ring aid is not qualified.
This disqualification was declared by the Grand Master in 1949 and
his decision was approved by the Grand Lodge.
It may be asserted that during the ensuing seventeen years the art of
miniaturizing of instruments , accelerated by the building of rockets. has
resulted in the development of some hearing aids which, batteries and
all. can be lodged in the ear canal and thus are, or are almost, undiscernable from the exterior, this factor alone is not conclusive that a change
should be made.
Your committee on Policy and General Purposes does recommend
that you change our law in this particular and prefers to base its conclusion upon not only the advances in the art o f manufacture of hearing
aids but upon the broader ground of internal qualifications weighed
against purely physical a ttributes. Your committee feels that issues as
to physical qualification must each be decided upon the particular impa irment involved. It has long been our law that there are some amputations and losses which do not disqualify an applicant and we deem that
the wearing of a modern hearing aid should now be moved over into
that classification.
We find grea t difficulty in discerning any substantial difference between an applicant who mus t wear a hearing aid and one who must rely
upon s trong corrective glasses. The fact that the latter may remove his
glasses affords no basis for a distinction.
We have taken into consideration the probability that one who wears
a hearing aid would not be embarrassed upon finding himself in the center
of a group, whereas. one who must wear an artificial limb and not knowing what would be required of him, suddenly finds himself in the center
of a group most of w hom are strangers .
We are authorized to state tha t the Committee on Ritual feels that
the questions involved are matters of policy and not of ritual. hence they
will give no separate report.
We believe that the disqualification presently existing should be re-

The Committee on Ritual:
Resolution No. 22 proposes that the Grand Lodge designate the
minimum requirements for a Bible being substituted in place of the regular Lodge Bible.
The Resolution contains three Whereas-es. followed by the Resolve
portion, and we propose to discuss them in order.
The first Whereas sta tes that from time to time a Gift Bible is presented to a Candidate upon his raising, and we agree that this practice
has been followed on occasions in some Lodges. However, in order to
put this is proper focus, it should be pointed out that it is not a general
practice, and we are persuaded that a canvass of our constituent Lodges
would reveal that such presentations are made at relatively few of our
candidates' degrees. It follows, then, that this Resolution is framed and
presented for the benefit of a relatively few of our Lodges and candidates.
The second Whereas spells out the reason for the Resolution being
presented: "A Brother coaching a Candidate thru the three degrees
wishes to have his candidate obligated upon the Gift Bible." We submit
that a Resolution based on what would appear to be a convenience to
satisfy the vanity of the Coaching brother, or any other Brother, is insufficient reason to warrant considera tion.
The third Whereas states that "It is the policy of the Ritual Committee that a Candidate may be obligated on a Gift Bible. if large
enough." We agree that this has been the attitude and requirement of
the Ritua l Committee, as custodian of the esoteric work of our Grand
Lodge, and in thi~ instance the emphasis must be placed on the concluding phrase, "if large enough." Grand Lecturers through the years have
ruled that a Gift Bible, if it is used to obligate the candidate, must be of
such size that it can conform to the requirements of our ritual. A small
sized Bible obviously cannot do so.
The Resolution proposes a specification for a Bible to qualif,y as
''large enough." We contend that a Bible of this specification does not
conform to the requirements of the Ritual.
(Note: The report outlined in detail the reasons why this specified
Bible did not conform to the requirements of our Ritual).
In order to present the Resolution for consideration, we move its
adoption, but strongly urge a "No" vote.
The Committee on Policy and General Purposes does not consider
that a change in policy is involved, it being a purely ritualistic ma tter.
A majority voted against the resolution.
(NOTE: By separate action of Grand Lodge authorization was granted
to expunge from the records, minutes and proceedings esoteric language relating to Resolution No. 22.)

NOTICE TO DELINQUENT MEMBER
(26)
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, Section No. 579 C.M.C. requires the Secretary to
notify any member who bas refused or neglected to pay his regular dues
during a period of twelve months and,
WHEREAS, this section requires that the notice be sent either by
certified or registered letter to the last known address and deliverable to
addressee on/ y and
WHEREAS, in the majority of cases the member is not at home a nd
the letter cannot be delivered, thus resulting in it finally being returned
to the sender, now therefore,
BE IT RESOLVED. that Section No. 579 C.M.C. be amended by
striking out the words "deliverable to addressee only" in line four ( 4)
which follows that part of sentence reading "registered letter or certified
mail." This line will then appear as follows, "registered letter or certified
mail deposited in the U.S . Post Office addressed to him at his last known
address."
Respectfully submitted,
RAYL. WHITNEY, P.M., No. 513
Referred to Committees on Jurisprudence, and on Policy and General
Purposes.

The Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
This Resolution provides that notice of dues delinquency may be
mailed by registered or certified mail, as presently required, but that Section 579 C .M.C. be so amended that the further requirement of "deliverable to add ressee only" be removed.
The purpose of this proposal is to increase the practical probability
that the registered or certified mail be received by the delinquent brother.
Extensive experience of Lodge secretaries has been that in a large num ber of cases under the present rule, where the notice is deliverable to the
addressee only, the delinquent member is at work when mail deliveries
are made at bis home. a nd the notice cannot be delivered. This results in

275

PROCEEDINGS OP THE

GRAND LODGE OF CALIFORNIA

multiplying the burdens on the secretaries, who then make other efforts
to reach the brother, and involves a considerable added cash outlay for
the Lodge.
Your Committee on Policy and General Purposes is of the opinion
that the proposed Resolution is meritorious and will in fact further the
purpose of reaching delinquent brethren and giving opportunity to remedy their delinquency. The Committee believes, however, that delinquency
notices should be sent with return receipts requested, in order that proof
of delivery to the place addressed may be available to the secretary concerned.
Consequently, I move the amendment of Resolution No. 26 by the
insertion of the words "with return receipt requested" following the
words "registered letter or certified mail."
I now move the adoption of Resolution No. 26, as amended, and your
Committee on Policy and General Purposes recommends a yes vote
thereon.
The Committee on Jurisprudence indicated its concurrence in the recommendation.
Adopted as amended 5/6 vote.

The Committee on Policy and General Purposes :
Resolution No. 28 seeks to add to Section 769 C.M.C. a provision
making it permissible for the Master or Secretary of a Lodge from which
a member has been suspended or expelled, having knowledge that said
member is also a member of an organization or organizations requiring
Masonic affiliation as a condition of membership, to notify (presumably
in writing) the presiding officer or Secretary of each such organization
of the fact of such expulsion or suspension. Provision is also made for
similar notice to be made upon restoration to members hip of such a member.
There have been instances when Masons suspended from their Lodge
for non-payment of dues have, either by ignorance or design, continued
their membership in a Masonic affiliated organization or organizations.
The Committee on Policy and General Purposes believes this proposal is desirable and that use of such permissive procedure may help
materially in being certain that all Masons who are members of Masonic
affiliated organizations are also members in good standing of a Blue
Lodge. The Committee on Jurisprudence will present the necessary legis lation and the Committee on Policy and General Purposes recommends
a yes vote.

To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge F. 6 A . M. of California:
WHEREAS. all legislative, executive and judicial power of "The
Most Worshipful Grand Lodge of Free and Accepted Masons of the
State of California" is extended to the voting members of Grand Lodge
as set forth in Section 16 of the California Masonic Code; and
WHEREAS, the transaction of business in Grand Lodge is upon
written resolution and the present voting requirements under Section 782
of the California Masonic Code requires a five-sixths or 83.YJ % vote to
approve any resolution resulting in one-sixth or l 6YJ % vote governing
the transaction of business, such voting percentages having made it difficult if not impossible to enact popular resolutions and to disapprove
unpopular decisions, resulting in Grand Lodge having little value as a
legislative body; and

278

PROCEEDINGS OF THE

GRANO LODGE OF CALIFORNIA

WHEREAS. the Grand Lodge is based upon democratic principles
and its early leaders were largely responsible for the American system
of government wherein a majority or a % vote is required for passage
of legislation ; and
WHEREAS, it is believed that it is desirable tha t no greater voting
requirement be required of members of Grand Lodge than members of
Federal or State Government and that the Ordina nces of Grand Lodge
should be amended to make uniform such voting procedures in our Masonic Bodies;
NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that Section 782 of the
California Masonic Code should be amended as follows: (Bold Face
delete. Underline add).
SECTION 782. Vote required. Upon report of said committee, if
five-sixths two-thirds of the votes shall be in favor of such proposed

tion or report or the reversal of a decision or the rescision of a resolution
only required a majority vote.
The Ross Digest, adopted in 1931 , consisted of a constitution and a
new division denominated " ordinances of the Grand Lodge." The digest
in section 27 required a five-sixths vote to amend the constitution and in
section 349 laid down the same rule as to amendment of the ordinance
sections. These were carried over into the present code as sections 76
and 782.
Whether there were valid reasons for enacting section 349 of the
Ross Digest in 1931, need not be debated now. Since 1931 a substantial
change has been made as to the presentation and circulation of proposed
amendments to the ordinances. In 1931 and until 1956, proposed amendments to the ordinances might be presented on the opening day of a communication. No prior information thereon to the cra ft was required.
Since 1956 the requirement that proposed a mendments be filed 90
days and copies be distributed to the craft 60 days before a communication is a far better safeguard against ill advised action than the difference
between a two-thirds and a five-sixths vote.
If 66% percentage of those present and voting at any Communication
desire an amendment to an existing ordinance, your Committee on Policy
and General Purposes can find no logical reason why the vote of 17%
should delay action for one year (after which year, under our existing
law, that same vote, 66% % yes, is sufficient to adopt the amendment).
A two to one favorable vote should be sufficient the first time.
We are authorized to state on behalf of the Committee on Jurisprudence, that the la~guage of the proposed amendment, if adopted, will
accomplish the intended purpose.
I move the adoption of resolution number 29 and the Committee on
Policy and General Purposes recommends a yes vote.
A simple majority voted for the resolution. Failing a 5/ 6 vote, the
matter was held over until the 1967 Annual Communication as a "Proposed Amendment to the Ordinances." (Sec. 783 C.M.C.)

The Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
Resolution 29 proposes an amendment to section 782 of the California M asonic Code. If adopted, the present requirement of a five-sixths
affirmative vote to amend an ordinance would be reduced to a two-thirds
requirement. To state the matter in precentages, the present requirement
for an adoption on the first presentation of a proposed amendment is that
83 J1 % of the votes cast must be "yes." The resolution, if adopted, would
require that the affirmative vote be at least 66% % "yes."
It is important to bear in mind that the California Masonic Code as
the Ross Digest which preceded it, is composed of two parts, denominated " Constitution of the Grand Lodge of California" and "Ordinances
of the Grand Lodge of California." Resolution 29 does not propose any
change in the requirement of a five-sixths favorable vote in order to
amend the constitution; it would change the required vote only as to
proposed amendments to the ordinances.
From the founding of our Grand Lodge in 1850 until 1931. a span
of eighty-one years, the law of this jurisdiction consisted of ( 1} a constitution and ( 2) those decisions of G rand M asters which had been approved by the Grand Lodge and resolutions and reports which had been
adopted by the Grand Lodge. This latter category of course comprised
the larger portion of our law. The constitution, for the adoption of a
new section or the a mendment or repeal of an existing section, required
a five-sixth vote. The approval of a decision, the adoption of a resolu-

The proponents of Resolution Number 29 have also presented Resolution Number 30. By this Resolution, they propose to amend Section
783 by striking the words "two-thirds" and substituting the words "majority."
Section 782, which we have just discussed, precribes the vote required
to adopt a proposed amendment to the ordinances when it is first presented. Section 783 reads: "If the vote in favor of such proposed amendment
be less than that named in the preceding section, but there be a majority
therefor, it shall lie over for one year and shall be published with the
Proceedings, under the caption of 'Proposed Amendment to the Ordinances;' and if, at the next succeeding Annual Communication, it shall
receive two-thirds of the votes given thereon, it shall be declared adopted

..

In discussing the preceeding section it was noted that in 1931 when
Sections 782 and 783 were first enacted, there was no provision for advance notice or circularization of proposed amendments prior to the first
consideration thereof. You will note that the section we are. now consi<;lerin9 required the publication and circularizing of any amendment

GRAND LODGE OF CALIFORNIA

281

which failed to receive a five-sixths favor~ble. vote, bu~ di.d r~ceive a
majority vote. Obviously, the fact of pubhc~t1on and d1str1but1on was
deemed a sufficient reason to lower the required favorable vote on the
second consideration to two-thirds of those cast.
In the opinion of your Committee on Policy and General P urposes
the mere fact that previously there was a difference between the required
vote on the first and second considerations does not tend to prove that
there should be now a lowering on the second consideration from twothirds to a majority. On the contrary we are persuaded that the required
vote on the second consideration should be the same beca use now the
conditions as to notice and distribution before each ·c onsideration are
substantially the same. It does not appear to us tha t the mere fact that
a proposed amendment lays over for a year because it received a majority vote. is any reason why it should be adopted upon a lesser vote at
the second consideration.
We do feel that Section 783 in its present form serves a useful and
proper purpose in that it keeps a proposed amendment "alive," so to
.
.
.
speak. and insures a second consideration.
We are authorized to state that the Committee on Jurisprudence 1s
of the opinion that the language of the proposed amendment is sufficient,
if adopted. to accomplish the purpose of its proponents.
I move the adoption of Resolution 30 and the Committee on Policy
and General Purposes recommends a no vote.
A majority voted against the resolution.

MASTER MASON'S EMBLEM
(31)
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge F. 6 A. M. of California:
WHEREAS this Grand Lodge has prescribed Jewels of Grand
Master, Past Grand Master and Past Master and also provided for Gold
Buttons for Veteran Master Masons, and
WHEREAS the Square and Compass with letter "G" is and has
been accepted as a Masonic or Master Mason emblem or jewel throughout the world by Masons and profane, including the Lodges and Members of this Jurisdiction. on buildings. signs. printing and jewelry. therefore
BE IT RESOLVED that the Square and Compass with letter "G"
in an upright position to the viewer be accepted and recognized as a
Masonic or Master emblem. or jewel, by this Grand Lodge and the Ritual
Committee be directed to design and prescribe the form thereof.
}AMES B. WHITEHEAD, P.M., No. 402
P ERCY E. PALMER, P.M., No. 402
Referred to Committees on Policy and General Purposes, and on
Ritual.

282

PROCEEDINGS OP THE

The Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
Your Committee on Policy and General Purposes. to whom Resolution No. 31 entitled Master Mason's Emblem has been referred, reports
as follows :
This resolution appears to attempt to establish in our ordinances the
fact that we accept and recognize the Square and Compass with the
letter "G" as a Masonic or Master Mason emblem or jewel.
As recorded in the Appendix of the C.M.C .. on April 4, 1956. Grand
Lodge received a judgment in the Superior Court of the City and County
of San Francisco. In its judgment the court found that the Grand Lodge
has been continuously. since organization in 1850, and is now, the owner
of and entitled to use the Masonic emblem consisting of the square and
compass.
In addition, your Committee feels that after 115 years of common acceptance of such an emblem by the Grand Lodge of California and the
public at large, that any further or more formal establishment of the
emblem is unnecessary.
The resolution also calls for a direction to the Ritual Committee to
" design and prescribe the form thereof." The only purpose your Committee can assign to this provision is that of possible standardizing the
emblem to the point of rendering obsolete the prevailing emblems on our
temples, jewels. stationery. etc. We fail to see what good this would
accomplish . The Committee on Jurisprudence authorizes us to state that
they find no legal problem to be involved in the resolution.
The Committee on Ritual concurs in this report.
I. therefore, move the adoption of the resolution but the Committee on
Policy and General Purposes recommends a no vote.
A majority voted against the resolution.

WHEREAS. the Masonic Fraternity has always cherished ~nd encouraged the public schools system in the United ?tales of America. and
has regarded it as the foundation of the country s ?reatn.ess; and
WHEREAS. the future conduct of this country s ~ffairs depends on
the abilities and knowledge acquired by the youth of this country through
their attendance at the public schools and the application thereof to such
affairs; and
WHEREAS. it is believed that this Grand Lodge should institute an
annual program of financial assistance, for the benefit of. sue~ students
of the public high schools throughout the State. of Cahforma a~ may
desire to participate therein, through the establishment of a series of
scholarships available to members of the graduating classes of the several
public high schools throughout the state. regardless of sex. race, color or
creed ; and
WHEREAS. it is further believed that the Grand Lo~ge Committee
on Public Schools. in conjunction with its activities regard.mg th~ an~ual

said Committee should so determine). the cost of the prograi:n ~o ?e

such payments to be segregated in a separate fund to be known as the

contestants; and

five ( 5) remaining contestants in each of the six ( 6) Masonic Districts;
( 6) The necessary expenses to enable each winning contestant to
receive the award shall be paid by Grand Lodge from said Public Schools
Scholarship Fund;
( 7) All awards shall be announced at the next following convocation
of Grand Lodge and be paid in lump sum to the parents or guardians of
the winners. or in such other manner as they may request. with the understanding that such award shall be used for the furtherance of the education of the contestant;
NOW. THEREFORE. BE IT RESOLVED :
First - That this Grand Lodge hereby endorses and approves the
proposal to offer such scholarships on an annual basis;
Second - That the Committee on Public Schools is hereby authorized. empowered, and directed to prepare and institute a program of

(39)
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, there has been a great deal of confusion as to whether
or not Lodges and other Masonic organizations could hold dinners,
dinner dances and other social events in hotels and restaurants and as
to whether or not Masonic groups were able to follow the usual social
customs at such affairs; and
WHEREAS. it appears that this confusion should be eliminated and
that Masons and Masonic groups should be able to hold such gatherings
which could be conducted in the same manner as other people;
NOW, THEREFORE. BE IT RESOLVED. that the following
section be added to the California Masonic Code:
"Section 324.2. Social and other gatherings and meetings. A
Masonic Lodge, or an organization the prerequisite of membership wherein is that a person be a Master Mason, may hold social
gatherings, dinners, dinner dances, or other social events, or may
hold an open installation ofofficers, in a hotel. restaurant or other
establishment serving liquor or operating a bar; provided, however, in case of an open installation of a Masonic Lodge, the
Grand Master must first approve the location as suitable to the

Section 515.2. All Masons within the ter,ritorial jurisdiction of

(41)
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, it is the duty and obligation of all Master Masons
within the jurisdiction of the Grand Lodge of California to abide by all
rules and regulations set down by the California Masonic Code; and
WHEREAS, we find such code is outdated, in some respects, with
the civilian laws of the land; and
WHEREAS, we find our own members, and those interested in
membership in our Fraternity, wondering what is wrong with Masonry
that we have laws that are contrary to the recognized way of living
today; and

293

PRO CEEDINGS OP THE

GRAND LODGE OP CALIFORNIA

WHEREA S, we find that we are not only out of step with normal
habits of the population as a whole. but we find that other jurisdictions
do not follow our pattern regarding some phases of our laws, and
WHEREA S, we find it is a popular consensus of opinion among our
membership that some of our laws should be modernized to conform
with our modern way of life.

SERVING LIQUOR S-WEDD INGS AND
SOCIAL AFFAIRS IN MASONIC TEMPLES
(42)
To the Most Worshipful Grand lodge F. & A. M. of California:

WHEREA S, the passing of time has brought about a change in the
law and opinion of proper social and moral conduct in relation to the
serving and consumption of spirituous, malt or fermented liquor; and
WHEREAS . decisions of Grand Masters over the years have been
based on our existing laws that may prove to be obsolete thus making
them contradictor y to the fraternal and membership interest: and
WHEREA S, it is that restraint be exercised on some occasions but
that the intent should be confined to regular Blue Lodge meetings and
the regular meetings of Concordant Bodies of Masonry;
BE IT THEREFO RE RESOLVE D. that a temple may be rented
for the purpose of a wedding reception or other social affairs where
spirituous, malt or fermented liquors will be served, provided no regular
meeting of a Blue Lodge or Concordant Body is being held at the same
time;
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVE D, that all references contained in
our laws, rules, regulations, edicts. decisions or any other matter on this
subject, written or unwritten, having the force of law, which are contrary
hereto are rescinded.
Respectfully submitted,
GEORGE C. CouRREGES , P .M .• No. 349
Referred to Committees on Jurisprudenc e, and on Policy and General
Purposes.
The above resolution was withdrawn by its proponent.

WHEREA S, the passing of time has brought about a change in the
law and opinion of proper social and moral conduct in relation to the
serving and consumption of spirituous, malt or fermented liquors; and
WHEREA S, decisions of Grand Masters over the years have been
based on our existing laws that may prove to be obsolete thus making
them contradictor y to the fraternal and membership interest; and
WHEREA S. it is that restraint be exercised on some occasions but
that the intent should be confined to regular Blue Lodge meetings and
the regular meetings of Concordant Bodies of Masonry.
BE IT THEREFO RE RESOLVE D. that at all social gatherings
where a regular meal is being served that a social or fellowship hour be
allowed, (not to exceed one hour) and may be held wherever the
civilian laws will permit; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVE D. that all references contained in
our laws, rules, regulations, edicts, decisions or any other matter on this
subject, written or unwritten, having the force of law, which are contrary
hereto are rescinded.

SERVING LIQUOR S-BANQ UET OR SOCIAL
ROOMS OF MASONIC TEMPLES
(44)
To the Most Worshipful Grand lodge F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREA S, Masonic Lodges de.rive a portion of their operating
revenue from the rental of their banquet and social rooms; and
WHEREA S. many Masonic Lodges are largely dependent upon
and greatly in need of the revenues from aforesaid rentals; and
WHEREA S. said Lodges are in need of additional and greater
revenues from the rental of aforesaid facilities for the purposes of meeting the demands of operating expense; and
WHEREAS . the present restrictive provisions of Section 199k of
the California Masonic Code discourages the rental of the aforesaid
facilities by many non-Masoni c individuals. groups and organization s
by reason of the fact that these gatherings customarily serve some
alcoholic beverages in moderate amounts; and
WHEREAS . unless said individuals. groups and organization s are

29i

PROCEEDINGS OF THE

permitted to serve some alcoholic beverages in moderate amounts at
their functions and gatherings. they will be disinclined to rent the aforesaid facilities with the resultant loss of substantial and needed revenue to
the Lodges: now, therefore,
BE IT RESOLVED that Section 199h be rephrased to read "a
temple may not be rented for a lunch or dinner after which bingo or
whist is to be played for prizes." and that Section 199k of the California
Masonic Code be repealed and the following provisions be substituted
in its stead:
a) A Masonic Temple Association, Corporation, Lodge, or group
of Masons shall not, under any conditions or circumstances.
permit or allow, either by lease or otherwise, any person, association, group, lodge, society or organization to use any part
or portion of a Masonic Temple for the purpose of selling
intoxicating liquor therein or thereon , or for holding any meeting or gathering where intoxicating liquor is to be sold.
b) In no event shall alcoholic beverages be permitted on the
premises at a time when any Masonic or related function is
taking place.
c) Alcoholic beverages may be permitted only within the banquet
or social rooms of a Masonic Temple and in no event within
a Lodge Room.

EMERGENT RESOLUTION
Upon consent of five-sixths vote of the members present, the Grand
Master declared the following resolution emergent and subject to consideration at this communication:

ANNUAL COMMUNICATION DATE
To the M ost Worshipful Grand Lodge F. & A. M . of California:
RESOLVED: That Section 101 of the California Masonic Code be
amended to read as follows:
"Section 101. Annual. Each Annual Communication shall be
held in the City and County of San Francisco, commencing on the
third Monday of October, at ten o'clock A.M .. provided, however, that any Annual Communication may be held at any other
place in the State of California upon adoption by this Grand
Lodge at any previous Communication by a five-sixths vote of a
resolution so providing."
Respectfully submitted.
Members of Board of Trustees
California Masonic Memorial Temple
Referred to Committees on Jurisprudence, and on Policy and General
Purposes.
A member of the Board of Trustees of the California Masonic
Memorial Temple spoke in favor of the resolution and urged a yes vote.
The Chairman of the Committee on Policy and Gl?neral Purposes
spoke against the resolution and urged a no vote. The Committee on
Jurispruden ce indicated the wording of the resolution, if adopted, would
accomplish the purpose intended.
A majority voted against the resolution.

REPORT OF COMMITTEE ON FINANCE
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge F. & A. M. of California:
At the close of the 1965 Communication of this Grand Lodge, and in
accordance with policy as to Committee Structure adopted at the 1964
Communication, the then Chairman of the Committee on Finance, Past
Grand Master Frank Harwell. Jr. , announced his retirement as Chairman and member of the Committee, he having served as such from the
close of the 1954 Communication. a period of eleven ( 1 I) years. These
were years of valuable service rendered by a dedicated Mason, well
versed in the field of finance and investments. The strong financial condition of this Grand Lodge is testimony to the leadership afforded by
Frank Harwell, Jr. Within the short period of three months from his
retirement from the Committee, he was summoned from his earthly
labors to the Supreme Grand Lodge on High. and your present Com~
mittee pauses in these few words to pay just tribute to a beloved companion and leader.

In accordance with the requirement of the California Masonic Code,
an audit of the finances of Grand Lodge and its agencies for the fiscal
year ended June 30. 1966, has been completed. Copies of the several
reports comprising the audit have been examined by the members of this
Committee and it is our opinion that the reports correctly state the
financial position of Grand Lodge.
It is most interesting, and gratifying. to note an over-all improvement in the financial picture of Grand Lodge and its agencies - this
notwithstandin g a somewhat turbulent year in the financial world, and
otherwise.
For the fiscal year under review. the budget for 1965-1966 anticipated
total income of $426.000 and total appropriations , or disbursements, of
$404 ,584. leaving an estimated excess of receipts over disbursements,
of $21.416. Against these budgeted figures, total income was $438 ,743
and total disbursements were $386.661. Receipts for the fiscal year were
up $12,743 and expenses were down $19.500, providing a cash. ~urplus
before capital disbursements, of some $30.000 higher than ant1c1pated .
this before considering the cost of producing the California Freemason.
The budget for the California Freemason, based on estimates of
$60.273 for revenue and $60,900 for expenses. was not sufficient and a
substantial deficit occurred for reasons explained in a subsequent section
of this report. With total expenses of $89,996. thedeficit for the California Freemason proved to be $29,722. This sum. plus $4.926 spent for
capital items, served to reduce the cash surplus remaining in the budget
at June 30. 1966, to $17,434.
As in former ·y ears, the Grand Secretary and his staff of employees
have rendered competent, conscientious service in the administering of
their duties. Their loyalty to Grand Lodge communicates to Grand
Lodge officers and committeemen and materially contributes to the
favorable financial reports which are being presented.
GRANO TREASURER'S REPORT

The Grand Treasurer's Report was referred to and examined by this
Committee. Not only do the items having to do with Finance tie in with
the Audit, but the report contains much of interest to the Craft in matters
of Grand Lodge investments and the financial details of Grand Lodge
agencies. The keen interest of the Grand Treasurer in all things appertaining to Freemasonry and Grand Lodge, coupled with his known abilities in the business and financial worlds, make him a great asset to this
Committee and to the Fraternity. We recommend approval of his report.

"CALIFORNIA FREEMASON" MAGAZINE

A second year has now ended during which our quarterly magazine
has been furnished free to all regular members of Lodges in this Jurisdiction. Previous reports indicated the difficulty, even impossibility, of
determining the exact per capita sum necessary to cover the cost of publishing and distributing the magazine for any one year. The deficit for
the year ended was occasioned substantially by inventorying paper stock
to be used during the current Grand Lodge Year.
It is apparent, however, from figures now available, that a year's expenses, based on current costs and the new plan of editorship proposed
by the Editor-in-Chie f, Judge Newcomb Con dee, will require a 1Oc per
capita increase to- the sum of $.35. Su ch a per capita, based on a membership of 240.000. will produce revenue of $84.000 against estimated
expenses of $81,000, and your C ommittee on Finance so recommends .

The gradual. but noticeable improvement, in the Grand Lodge
Library on the second floor of this building requires additional cabinets
from time to time. A program designed to improve the use and attractiveness of the Masonic Temple at Columbia is being carried forward. New,
and necessary. equipment in the Grand Lodge office is provided for in
this budget. The cost of these programs for the current fiscal year,

UNITED GRAND LoDGE OP ENGLAND
On June 27, 1967, the United Grand Lodge of England is holding a
special communication to celebrate the completion of two hundred and
fifty years since the founding of the United Gra~d Lodge of England.
It is the desire of its Grand Master that all recognized Grand Lodges the
world over be represented at the special Communication by their Grand
Masters and Grand Secretaries. accompanied by their ladies. and. accordingly. this Grand Lodge has received such an invitation. We have
been favored on special occasions by visits of Grand Lodge officers
from the British Isles and from other Grand Lodges around the world.
We have welcomed these visits as being in the best interests of Freemasonry. Feeling that it will be the desire of the brethren of this Grand
Lodge that we be represented when the mother Gr.and L~ge celebra~es
the 250th anniversary of its existence. the Committee on Finance has included in the budget the sum of $4.500 for the purpose of sending our
Grand Master and Grand Secretary, together with their wives, to the
communication in London, England. We recommend approval of this
item.
SALARIES
. During the last two fiscal years, 1964-1965 and 1965-1966, the
budget for salaries remained the same and, in each of the two years,

GRANO LODGE OP CALIFORNIA

299

actual salaries paid were approximately $8,000 less than the budgeted
amounts.
Notwithstanding this favorable fact, we are increasing the budget
for salaries this year from $93,000 to $98.000. This is a modest increase
to enable the Grand Secretary to make such salary adjustments as he
deems advisable for employees other than himself in the Grand Lodge
office.
Coupled with compensation for employees in this day and time are
the related subjects of retirement and medical benefits. Grand Lodge and
the Masonic Homes instituted such plans some years ago. The plans have
and are benefiting employees for whom they were intended and they
will be used more extensively in years to come. These plans enable us
to be competitive in the labor market for the type of employee we seek.
It has been apparent that our plans were somewhat outmoded and
that they needed improving. Studies were made by our actuaries and
their recommendations were adopted by the Retirement Plan Committee
and the Trustees of the Masonic Homes of California. The proposed
budget reflects the increase in premium costs by reason of up-dating the
Retirement Pension Plan.
CALIFORNIA ·MASONIC MEMORIAL TEMPLE
Your Committee on Finance shares with all members of Grand

cannot be given those who led us in the building and financing of this
Temple and to the members of the Craft who assumed the burden of
the $1.00 per capita tax which has now been removed by action of this
Grand Lodge.

PRO CEEDINGS OF THE

In analyzing the budget, it is readily noticeable that expenses have
increased. Salary adjustments are necessary and provision has been
made for increases which will total approximately $5,000.00. Charges
to Grand Lodge for office space and other services are estimated to increase $6.000.00. The balance in a substantial reserve in the Retirement
Plan, not used at the time of death of Lloyd E. Wilson, Past Grand
Secretary. has now been applied to premiums due in succeeding years.
Annual premium costs for Grand Lodge and Grand Lodge Agencies
employees will now increase by approximately $8.500.00 due to the
up-dating of the Retirement Plan and the using of reserves. A Personal
Property Tax on equipment belonging to Grand Lodge has now been
levied .a nd you will find a new expense item of $1.020.00 in this connection. A non-recurring item in the budget is the appropriation of
$4.500.00 for our delegates to the 250th Communication of the Grand
Lodge of England.
It is now necessary that the blanket Public Liability Policy handled
by Grand Lodge for all but eleven of its 711 Lodges be re-written to
include all Lodges. Grand Lodge formerly paid a three year premium
in advance on behalf of covered constituent Lodges and then billed
each covered Lodge for its proportionate share of the total premium at
the end of each year of the three year coverage. said billing including
a charge of $.0125 per capita for necessary premium financing and
bookkeeping services.
The new plan, now to be inaugurated, will accomplish several things.
The annual billing to Lodges will be eliminated because the proportionate share of each Lodge in the premium cost of the master policy
will be returned to Grand Lodge in the form of a per capita tax. For
example, constituent Lodges will not have to pay an insurance bill in
December, 1966. inasmuch as the new per capita incorporated in this
budget will not be payable until annual returns, for the year ending
June 30. 1967, are filed . For the reason that the new Public Liability
Policy to be written constitutes a true master policy, our insurance
counselor advises us that better protection can be obtained and at
more favorable rates. The policy will provide Public Liability with a
single $1 .000,000.00 limit including all legal liabilities. medical payment
benefits, broad form coverage on money and securities, and broad form
coverage on Lodge paraphernalia. The estimated annual per capita of
$.14 for this broadened and more complete coverage relates favorably
to your present costs.
To accomplish this revision, it is necessary to provide an additional
per capita of $.22 in this budget to take care of premium costs of approximately $53,000.00 for a nineteen months period, to be reduced to
a per capita of $.14 for twelve months of coverage in subsequent years.
assuming premium costs for this type of Public Liability insurance protection will remain stable.

GRAND LODGE OP CALIFORNIA

305

Again we state that actual costs to constituent Lodges will not be
increased through this procedural change; they should decrease. The
per capita servicing charge will be eliminated and there will be no insurance billings to Lodges to be paid in December, 1966.
Taken on the whole, the budget which we are presenting "holds the
line" compared to the budget for last year - excepting the items on
which we have just made special comment. We are confident that
those to whom will be intrusted the responsibility for the spending of
Grand Lodge funds will be ever conscious of their obligations to their
brethren .
We offer the following resolution, pointing out that the portion of
the total per capita, entitled "additional per capita for Grand Lodge,"
reflects a $.37 increase over last year and that it will provide a small
but, we hope. adequate cash surplus based on estimates of income and
expenses.
RESOLVED: That for the purposes of paying the expenses of
Grand Lodge, a per capita of $3.57 be levied for the fiscal year
ending June 30, 1967, d ivided as follows:
Masonic Homes ----------------·---··-------·······--·-·--······················-·····-$1.50

Additional per capita for Grand Lodge.................................. 1.22

Total Per Capita ................................................................ $3.57
Respectfully submitted,

Guv B. M1zE, Chairman

AFTERN OON SESSIO N-Friday , October 14, 1966
At 2:00 p.m. Grand Lodge was called on. the Grand Master presiding. This session was raised by Worshipf ul Bryant B. Hathaway,
Master of Calaveras Lodge No. 78. The Grand Chaplain delivered the

INST ALLATlON OF OFFICER S
Most Worshipf ul Ellsworth Meyer, Past Grand Master. acted as
Master of Ceremoni es and the officers, elected and appointed , were
installed by the retiring Grand Master in accordanc e with the Ritual.
The newly installed Grand Master invested his predecesso r with a
Past Grand Master's lapel button.
The Charles Albert Adams lapel pin was transferre d from the retiring to the incumbent Grand Master, and the other chair officers exchanged the Arthur S. Crites lapel pins.
Presented to the newly installed Grand Orator was the Everett
Houser lapel pin and the Robert B. Watts lapel pin was presented to
the newly installed Grand Chaplain on behalf of the retiring Grand
Chaplain by the Grand Master.
Most Worshipf ul Edgar V . Stewart, Jr. invested the retiring Grand
Master with the apron of his new designatio n and Most Worshipf ul
L. Harold Anderson presented a Past Grand Master's Pin. Laurence
E. Dayton, the newly installed Grand Master, then presented him with
a Past Grand Master Certificate .
A gift for Mrs. Smith was then tendered by the Grand Secretary on
behalf of the members of Grand Lodge. for which the junior Past Grand
Master expressed his gratitude and sincere appreciati on for having
served the Fraternity as its Grand Master.
Following the installatio n Most Worshipf ul Laurence E. Dayton
introduced to Grand Lodge members of his Lodge. He expressed his
feeling of humility in being elected to serve as Grand Master and urged
each member to increase his "candle power" so that the light and
strength of Freemaso nry would be seen and felt by all.
At 3 :20 p.m. all business being completed , Grand Lodge was closed
in due form.

portion thereof shall be expended for any purpose, and the income
therefrom shall be used only for the maintenance and general operation of the Masonic Homes.

The principal, res t ricted by the terms of the Will, is to be kept
intact and th e income used only for the benefit of the care of orph a ns
o r the aged in . Mason i c Homes of Southern California.

The financial statements are stated on a modified cash basis
of accounting. Transactions generally are recorded at the time of the
receipt or payment of cash. current operating expense bills unpaid
·were of nominal amount.
Land, buildings, and equipment are recorded at the cost when
originally purchased and no depreciation of buildings and equipment
has been provided for in the accounts. Replacements of original items
of equipment are charged to operating expenses.

Note 2.

Investments:

Investments in securities purchased are stated at cost.
Securities received by gift or bequest or by assignment by residents
of the Home at Decato are stated at estimated market value at the
time the securities are received or at the nominal value of $1 if the
market value is unknown. In a few instances, the carrying value of
unlisted stocks acquired by gift or bequest has been stated at the
per share value of the underlying assets of the company which is
believed to be less than the market value.
